migrate.title: Migrate from Mailchimp / Mandrill
migrate.lede: Keep sending through your existing Mailchimp Transactional account on day one — same reputation, same deliverability — while Owlat measures both senders on identical instrumentation and moves traffic onto its own MTA only as the numbers earn it. There is no flag day, and every step here is reversible.

connect.missing: Create an API key in Mailchimp Transactional (Settings → API keys), set it as {envVar} in this deployment's environment, and restart. Credentials never live in the database, so this page can only ever tell you whether the key is present — never what it is.

domain.none: No Mailchimp Transactional identity exists yet. Verify a sending domain on the domains screen first; enabling Mandrill as the fallback relay provisions the identity automatically, and the hourly sweep picks up the DNS from there.

sns.title: SES bounce & complaint feedback
sns.subtitle: Let SES tell Owlat when mail bounces or is marked as spam, so those addresses are suppressed automatically
sns.intro: SES delivers this feedback through an Amazon SNS topic. Point an HTTPS subscription at the endpoint below — Owlat verifies each message’s signature and confirms the subscription for you.
sns.noSiteUrl: Set your site URL to see the endpoint SNS should subscribe to.
sns.step1: In the SNS console, create a topic (e.g. {topic}) and add an {https} subscription with the endpoint above.
sns.step2: Set {envVar} to that topic’s ARN. Owlat only accepts feedback from this exact topic, so the endpoint stays closed until it’s set.
sns.step3: In the SES console, create a {configurationSet} with an event destination publishing {bounce}, {complaint} and {delivery} events to that topic.
sns.step4: Set {envVar} to the set’s name so every send is attributed. Changes take effect on the next send — no restart needed.
sns.noEvents: No feedback received yet. Once the subscription is confirmed and a message bounces or is delivered, it appears here.
